old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a golden-colored kettle placed on a gas stove burner. The kettle is filled with water that is visibly boiling, creating small bubbles and steam rising from the surface. The stove has a metallic finish with black grates, and the kettle is positioned on one of these burners. Surrounding the kettle, there is aluminum foil spread out on the stovetop to catch any spills or splashes. In the background, part of a kitchen counter is visible, featuring a blue bowl containing what appears to be rice and a small red chili pepper. The lighting in the scene is bright, highlighting the reflective surface of the kettle and the steam rising from the boiling water. There are no significant changes or movements throughout the sequence; the focus remains on the kettle and its contents as they continue to boil.

caption: The video captures a top-down close view of an open golden kettle with a black-gripped overhead handle resting on crinkled aluminium foil on a stovetop. To the left, a metal gas-hob grate with a black knob is visible, while white tiled walls, a small brown object, and a blue bowl of rice occupy the background. Inside the kettle, a dark reddish-brown liquid churns in a vigorous rolling boil, with bubbles forming, bursting, and steam drifting upward. The surface turbulence shifts constantly from frame to frame, yet the kettle, foil, and surrounding objects remain stationary. A fingertip appears briefly near the lower edge by the spout, withdraws, and later appears again, without moving the kettle. As the boiling continues, a yellowish-green solid mass becomes visible at the left side of the liquid, with the churning contents shifting. The view remains centered on this ongoing process, showing persistent bubbling, steam, and shifting liquid motion.

not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
